units.name: core
units.role: The `rg` command-line program: parses flags, wires the other units together, walks/searches files, and prints results.
units.description: This is the ripgrep application itself, the code that turns typed command-line flags into an actual search. It reads and validates every flag and config file the user supplies, decides whether to search sequentially or across many threads at once, asks the file-walking unit for a list of files, asks the matching-and-searching units to find matches in each file, and asks the printing unit to show the results (or the indexing unit, when the experimental index feature is used). It is the glue that makes a runnable program out of all the reusable library pieces.

entrypoints.name: main
entrypoints.plain: The program's starting point: run `rg` from a terminal and this is what runs first.

entrypoints.name: parse
entrypoints.plain: Reads the command-line arguments and any config file, and turns them into a validated set of search options.

entrypoints.name: HiArgs
entrypoints.plain: The fully resolved set of options for one run of ripgrep (what to search for, where, and how to display it), built from the raw flags.

entrypoints.name: SearchWorkerBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Configures and creates the object that actually searches one file and reports whether it matched.

entrypoints.name: HaystackBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Turns a raw directory-walk result into a concrete file that ripgrep is allowed to search.

effects.description: Opens the files it searches, reads pattern/config files (-f, RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH), and writes search results and statistics to stdout.
Spawns an external preprocessor command (--pre) to transform a file's contents before searching it, and shells out to `git rev-parse` at build time to embed a commit hash.
Reads environment variables such as RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH, NO_COLOR, PATH (to locate the preprocessor binary) and terminal-related variables that affect defaults.
Times how long a search takes (Instant::now) to report in --stats output.

units.name: cli
units.role: Reusable helpers for building search-oriented command-line tools: stdin detection, colored/buffered stdout, byte-safe escaping, pattern-file reading, decompression, and running child processes.
units.description: This unit is a small toolbox of utilities that any command-line search tool would need, not specific to grepping itself. It can tell whether the program's input or output is connected to a real terminal, it manages how colored output is buffered, it safely converts between raw bytes and printable escape sequences, it reads search patterns from files or stdin with good error messages, and it knows how to run another program (like `gzip` or `xz`) and stream its output back so ripgrep can search inside compressed files.

entrypoints.name: is_readable_stdin
entrypoints.plain: Tells the caller whether there is real piped-in data on stdin worth searching.

entrypoints.name: StandardStream
entrypoints.plain: A handle for writing colored output to the terminal that buffers efficiently whether or not it's connected to a real terminal.

entrypoints.name: stdout
entrypoints.plain: Gets a ready-to-use handle for writing colored results to standard output.

entrypoints.name: DecompressionReaderBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Configures a reader that transparently decompresses a file (gzip, xz, bzip2, ...) by running the matching external decompression program.

entrypoints.name: DecompressionReader
entrypoints.plain: A stream of decompressed bytes read from a compressed file, produced by running an external decompressor.

entrypoints.name: CommandReaderBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Configures a reader that runs an external command and streams its stdout, converting a failing exit code into a helpful error.

entrypoints.name: patterns_from_path
entrypoints.signature: pub fn patterns_from_path<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P) -> io::Result<Vec<String>>
entrypoints.plain: Reads a file of search patterns, one per line, for use with ripgrep's -f/--file flag.

entrypoints.name: pattern_from_os
entrypoints.plain: Validates that a pattern given on the command line is valid UTF-8, with a precise error if it isn't.

entrypoints.name: parse_human_readable_size
entrypoints.plain: Converts a size like "2M" typed on the command line into a plain byte count.

entrypoints.name: escape
entrypoints.plain: Turns arbitrary bytes into a printable, typeable escaped string for error messages.

entrypoints.name: hostname
entrypoints.plain: Looks up the current machine's hostname (used to build hyperlinks in output).

effects.description: Reads pattern files from disk (patterns_from_path) and writes buffered, optionally colored output to stdout.
Spawns external decompression programs (gzip, bzip2, xz, lz4, zstd, ...) and other child processes, and reads their stdout/stderr.
Consults the PATH environment variable to resolve which binary to run for a given decompression/preprocessor program.

units.name: globset
units.role: General-purpose glob and glob-set matching, independent of grep or gitignore semantics.
units.description: This unit compiles Unix-style wildcard patterns like '*.rs' or 'src/**/foo.rs' into fast matchers, and can test one or many such patterns against a file path at once, reporting which ones matched. It has no knowledge of grep, regular text search, or gitignore rules; it is a standalone, published library that both the file-type-filtering and gitignore-parsing units build on top of.

entrypoints.name: Glob
entrypoints.plain: A single compiled wildcard pattern, e.g. '*.rs'.

entrypoints.name: GlobBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Configures how a single glob pattern should be interpreted (case sensitivity, whether '*' can cross directory separators, etc.) before compiling it.

entrypoints.name: GlobMatcher
entrypoints.plain: A compiled single glob, ready to test candidate paths against.

entrypoints.name: GlobSet
entrypoints.plain: A compiled set of many glob patterns that can all be tested against one path in a single pass, returning which ones matched.

entrypoints.name: GlobSetBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Accumulates individual globs and compiles them into one efficient GlobSet.

entrypoints.name: Candidate
entrypoints.plain: A pre-processed path, used to match the same path against many globs cheaply.

units.name: grep
units.role: The 'ripgrep as a library' facade: a single crate that re-exports the matching, regex, pcre2, searching, printing and cli units under one name.
units.description: This unit does not contain search logic of its own. It is a thin convenience layer that gathers all of the separately published grep-* library crates (the matcher trait, the two regex engines, the line searcher, the result printers, and the cli helpers) and re-exports them under one crate called 'grep', so that a downstream program only has to depend on one thing. The core ripgrep application uses this facade rather than depending on each piece individually.

entrypoints.name: cli
entrypoints.signature: pub extern crate grep_cli as cli;
entrypoints.plain: Re-exports the command-line helper utilities (the 'cli' unit) for downstream users.

entrypoints.name: matcher
entrypoints.signature: pub extern crate grep_matcher as matcher;
entrypoints.plain: Re-exports the generic text-matching trait (the 'matcher' unit).

entrypoints.name: pcre2
entrypoints.signature: pub extern crate grep_pcre2 as pcre2;
entrypoints.plain: Re-exports the PCRE2-backed regex matcher (the 'pcre2' unit), only when the pcre2 feature is enabled.

entrypoints.name: printer
entrypoints.signature: pub extern crate grep_printer as printer;
entrypoints.plain: Re-exports the result printers (the 'printer' unit).

entrypoints.name: regex
entrypoints.signature: pub extern crate grep_regex as regex;
entrypoints.plain: Re-exports the Rust-regex-backed matcher (the 'regex' unit).

entrypoints.name: searcher
entrypoints.signature: pub extern crate grep_searcher as searcher;
entrypoints.plain: Re-exports the line-oriented file searcher (the 'searcher' unit).

units.name: ignore
units.role: Recursively walks a directory tree while filtering out files/directories per .gitignore, .ignore, global excludes and file-type rules.
units.description: This unit provides ripgrep's file discovery: given a starting directory, it walks the tree (optionally in parallel across many threads) and, for each entry, decides whether it should be skipped because it matches a .gitignore or .ignore rule, an explicit override, a hidden-file rule, or a file-type filter such as '--type rust'. It has no idea what a regular expression is; its only job is to produce the right list of files and directories to hand to the searching unit.

entrypoints.name: WalkBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Configures a recursive directory walk: which ignore files to respect, whether to follow symlinks, thread count, and so on.

entrypoints.name: Walk
entrypoints.plain: A single-threaded iterator over directory entries that respects the configured ignore rules.

entrypoints.name: WalkParallel
entrypoints.plain: A multi-threaded version of the directory walk, calling back into user code for each entry found.

entrypoints.name: DirEntry
entrypoints.plain: One file or directory found during the walk, along with its path and metadata.

entrypoints.name: Gitignore
entrypoints.plain: A compiled set of gitignore-style rules from one file, that can test whether a given path is ignored.

entrypoints.name: Types
entrypoints.plain: A compiled set of file-type definitions (e.g. what counts as a 'rust' or 'python' file) used by --type/--type-not.

entrypoints.name: TypesBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Accumulates and selects file-type definitions before compiling them into Types.

entrypoints.name: Override
entrypoints.plain: A set of user-supplied glob overrides (-g/--glob) that can force-include or force-exclude paths regardless of gitignore rules.

effects.description: Recursively reads directory entries, opens and parses .gitignore/.ignore files, and follows/detects symlinks while walking.
Consults environment/home-directory information to locate global gitignore and git config files.

units.name: index
units.role: Experimental on-disk search index (ngram-based) that lets ripgrep skip files that can't possibly match, backed by an embedded database.
units.description: This unit builds and reads a persistent index of file contents stored on disk, so that a later search can quickly discover which files are even worth opening instead of reading every file from scratch. It is currently unstable/opt-in and self-contained: it does not depend on ripgrep's own matching or searching code, only on generic external indexing and database libraries. The core application uses it, when enabled, as an alternative fast path before falling back to a normal file-by-file search.

entrypoints.name: Index
entrypoints.plain: A handle to an open on-disk search index for one directory.

entrypoints.name: IndexBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Creates or opens an on-disk index, in read-only or writable mode.

entrypoints.name: IndexDiscovery
entrypoints.plain: Searches upward from the current directory to find an existing index to use.

effects.description: Creates and opens an index directory containing an 'index.db' file on disk.
Reads and writes the index as an embedded redb key-value database file.
Reads environment/current-directory state while discovering an existing index.

units.name: matcher
units.role: Defines the generic 'Matcher' trait that every text-matching engine in ripgrep (Rust regex, PCRE2) implements, plus the shared Match/Captures types.
units.description: This unit defines the common language that all of ripgrep's search engines speak, independent of which actual regex library is used underneath. It describes, as a Rust trait, what it means to search a slice of bytes and report matches, capture groups and replacements. It contains no search implementation itself; the regex and pcre2 units each implement this trait, and the searcher and printer units are written generically against it so they work with either engine.

entrypoints.name: Matcher
entrypoints.plain: The shared interface every regex/text-matching engine in ripgrep implements, so the rest of the program doesn't need to care which engine is in use.

entrypoints.name: Match
entrypoints.plain: A start/end byte range identifying where a match was found.

units.name: pcre2
units.role: Implements the Matcher trait using the PCRE2 regex engine, enabling backreferences and lookaround that Rust's own regex engine doesn't support.
units.description: This unit adapts the third-party PCRE2 regular expression library so that it can be used anywhere ripgrep expects a Matcher. It is what powers ripgrep's optional '-P/--pcre2' flag, giving users access to advanced regex features like backreferences and lookaround at the cost of some performance, while presenting the exact same interface as the default regex engine to the rest of the program.

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcher
entrypoints.plain: A compiled PCRE2 regular expression that implements the shared Matcher interface.

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcherBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Configures PCRE2-specific options (case insensitivity, multi-line, JIT, ...) before compiling a pattern.

units.name: printer
units.role: Turns raw search matches into ripgrep's various output formats: human-readable (standard), JSON lines, and summary/count-only.
units.description: This unit is responsible for what the user actually sees after a search runs. It receives match events from the searcher unit and renders them as colorized human-readable text (the default), as newline-delimited JSON for machine consumption, or as an aggregate summary showing only match counts or matching file names. It also tracks statistics like elapsed time and bytes printed for ripgrep's --stats output.

entrypoints.name: Standard
entrypoints.plain: The default human-readable printer, similar to standard grep output, with optional color and context lines.

entrypoints.name: StandardBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Configures the standard printer's behavior (line numbers, context, color, replacement text, ...) before use.

entrypoints.name: JSON
entrypoints.plain: Prints one JSON object per line describing each match, for machine consumption.

entrypoints.name: Summary
entrypoints.plain: Prints only an aggregate result per file, e.g. just the count of matches or just the matching file names.

entrypoints.name: Stats
entrypoints.plain: Accumulated statistics (matches, lines, bytes, elapsed time) for the whole search, used by --stats.

entrypoints.name: PathPrinter
entrypoints.plain: Prints just a file path, used when ripgrep is only listing files rather than searching their contents.

entrypoints.name: ColorSpecs
entrypoints.plain: Holds the parsed --colors configuration describing what color/style to use for matched text, line numbers, etc.

effects.description: Measures elapsed search time (Instant::now) to include in JSON 'summary' and text 'elapsed_total' output.

units.name: regex
units.role: Implements the Matcher trait using Rust's own 'regex' engine, ripgrep's default and fastest search backend.
units.description: This unit adapts Rust's regex library so it can be used anywhere ripgrep expects a Matcher, translating between ripgrep's own pattern syntax extensions (like word boundaries and case-insensitivity flags) and the underlying regex engine's configuration. It is the default engine used for every ripgrep search unless the user explicitly asks for PCRE2.

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcher
entrypoints.plain: A compiled regular expression, using Rust's regex engine, that implements the shared Matcher interface.

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcherBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Configures regex options (case sensitivity, multi-line, word boundaries, literal detection, ...) before compiling a pattern.

entrypoints.name: Error
entrypoints.plain: A regex compilation error with a human-readable explanation of what's wrong with the pattern.

units.name: searcher
units.role: The core line-oriented search engine: reads a file (or memory-mapped bytes), runs a Matcher over it, and reports matches, context and line numbers to a Sink.
units.description: This unit is the heart of ripgrep's search: given anything that implements the Matcher interface and a source of bytes, it efficiently scans for matches line by line, handles multi-line matches, counts lines, detects and skips binary files, shows surrounding context lines, and decides when to memory-map a file for speed. Results are reported by calling into a caller-supplied Sink, which is what the printer unit implements to actually display them.

entrypoints.name: Searcher
entrypoints.plain: Runs a search of a file or byte slice using a given Matcher and reports results to a Sink.

entrypoints.name: SearcherBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Configures search behavior before building a Searcher: context lines, binary detection, memory-map policy, multi-line mode, and more.

entrypoints.name: Sink
entrypoints.plain: The interface a Searcher calls into whenever it finds a match or context line, so results can be displayed or collected.

effects.description: Opens files as std::fs::File and, when enabled, memory-maps them with memmap2 for faster scanning.
